current.text: A Pelicans beat reporter expects Yves Missi to start at center over Queen.
Experts expect Queen to come off the bench and share the second unit. They call this bad for his value.
Experts agree that Queen and Zion Williamson fit poorly together, which limits how long they can share the floor.
New Orleans has more rotation players than minutes. Murray, Murphy, Jones, Zion, Missi, Fears, Bey, Mathurin and Queen all want playing time.
Jamahl Mosley is the new head coach, and Queen's minutes depend on how he handles the Queen and Zion frontcourt.
Experts see real upside if Queen wins the starting center job or Zion misses time. One expert put his ceiling at top 50 in that case. Josh thinks the Pelicans will rest Zion often.
Josh moved Queen down his board and calls his draft spot a little early if he comes off the bench. In an auction mock, Josh called a 6 USD price for Queen reasonable.
Queen is a risky pick. He is fine as a flyer but not as a sure starter.

durable.text: Queen is a hub big who works from the elbows and the free throw line. He is not a three-point spacer and makes very few threes.
He gives a broad counting line for a big: rebounds, assists well above his position, steals and blocks.
His turnovers are high for a forward or center.
He does not give the field goal percentage boost managers usually want from a center.
He is a poor defender and gives little rim protection.
His production comes in bursts. He has had poor first halves and big fourth-quarter runs.

note: Queen's market price is 3 to 4 USD (Yahoo rank 100, ESPN rank 89). Josh called 6 USD reasonable in a mock auction. He was not drafted in our league last season. As a bench big he is a cheap late buy for punt TO or punt 3PM builds, since he still adds rebounds, assists, steals and blocks from a F/C slot. Early in the season, check whether Missi keeps the starting job, how Mosley splits minutes between Queen and Zion, and whether Queen gets above his 25 minutes of last season.
